A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same work, algorithms and theoretical guarantees. The complete main texts, equations, algorithm displays and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 presents algorithms, theoretical bounds and proofs, including Appendices A–B. It reports no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical throughout. The Bernoulli instances in new Appendix A.4 are proof constructions, not reported simulations or empirical results.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain their objectives, sampling procedures, estimators, oracle calls and updates. Presenting contextual combinatorial semi-bandits (CCSB) before list classification does not change the proposed methods.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or benchmarks. CCSB, list classification and the single-label special case were already covered theoretically in v2.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. EXP4 and other prior methods remain analytical reference points rather than experimental comparators.

E3.justification: No experimental protocols are introduced or revised. The algorithm parameters and PAC sampling prescriptions are retained; the new lower-bound restrictions concern theoretical assumptions, assessed under T1.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, error analyses or case studies. Appendix A.4 adds mathematical analysis rather than a supplementary experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical run counts, seeds, error bars or significance tests. Confidence parameters and concentration inequalities occur within theoretical guarantees and proofs.

E6.justification: The headline PAC sample-complexity and adversarial-regret rates remain unchanged, and no measured numerical or qualitative outcomes are added. The new lower-bound derivation is assessed under T1.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.4 adds a formal lower-bound statement, revised Bernoulli construction, KL/Pinsker argument and sparsity-conditioning argument where v2 supplied only a sketch. Its Theorem 5 requires m <= K/12 rather than the retained Theorem 2's m <= K/2, and conditioning additionally requires s >= 4 log(2T). Existing upper-bound and regret proofs are unchanged apart from renumbering.

C1.justification: v3 emphasizes CCSB, but v2 already claimed the same general scope, oracle efficiency, sparsity-dependent rates, single-label improvement and adversarial-regret guarantee. The headline lower-bound claim also remains unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly clarifies that its L1 reward bound is weaker than requiring at most s nonzero coordinates. It removes v2's explanation that treating each list as one label destroys reward sparsity. The open problems concerning full-bandit feedback, dependence on K and infinite classes remain.

D1.justification: Algorithm pseudocode, ERM-oracle specifications, parameter choices and computational-complexity information are retained. No implementation resources, code/data access instructions or hardware details are added.

R1.justification: v3 adds Langford and Zhang (2007) for the recommendation-system motivation. Other cited works are retained, while the discussion of Erez et al. (2024b) shifts to contextual-bandit and policy-class terminology.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution summary and conclusion are revised around CCSB. Related-work paragraphs are reordered, and the separate classification/CCSB setups become a general setup followed by the classification special case. An acknowledgments section is added.

P2.justification: The expanded title and reorganized text reflow equation and paragraph blocks, and Appendix A.4 adds further mathematical displays. The same four algorithm displays retain their design; neither version contains figures or result tables.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies the existing CCSB scope and adds a detailed argument for the previously sketched lower bound. However, Appendix A.4 has narrower conditions than the retained Theorem 2 and asserts an unsupported E0[N_y] <= 3T/K counting bound despite mT total arm pulls. The exposition gains and unresolved proof problems leave the net quality effect uncertain.
